summary: Defines the Ghostbusters Record, a signed object holding contact details for the person responsible for an RPKI certificate. Resource certificates themselves hide names, so a contact is needed for problems such as expiry. The data is a severely profiled vCard. Its status is historic.

plainLanguage.summary: A certificate has no phone number on it. If it breaks, who do you call? This defines a signed contact card, named for the movie. It is now historic.

questions: how to contact an rpki certificate holder
what is the rpki ghostbusters record
how do you contact an rpki certificate holder
subtitle: A signed contact record for RPKI certificate maintainers, humorously named.

tldr.problem: RPKI certificates use abstract identifiers and hide human-readable names for security. When a certificate expires or breaks, there is no way to contact the person responsible for fixing it.
tldr.mechanism: The Ghostbusters Record is a signed object containing a profiled vCard with contact details (name, email, phone, address, organization). It is issued by the certificate maintainer and published alongside their resource certificates.
tldr.outcome: The RFC was published as Standards Track but is now Historic. Operators can use Ghostbusters Records to provide contact information for their RPKI assets, though adoption has been limited.

today: RFC 6493 is now Historic. While published as Standards Track, it has seen limited operational deployment. Operators can publish Ghostbusters Records to provide contact information for their RPKI CA certificates, but adoption remains optional and sparse in the global RPKI.

sections.title: The Problem: No Contact Information in RPKI Certificates
sections.content:
The Resource Public Key Infrastructure (RPKI) uses certificates to authenticate Internet routing information. These certificates contain abstract identifiers and no human-readable names. If a certificate expires, is about to expire, or has a stale Certificate Revocation List (CRL), the operator of the affected address space must contact the certificate maintainer to resolve the problem.

However, the certificate itself provides no way to identify or reach that person. The IESG asked: "Who you gonna call?" The answer is the Ghostbusters Record, named after the 1984 movie.
sections.plainLanguage: Imagine a lock on a safe with no label saying who can open it. If the lock breaks, you have no way to find the owner.

sections.title: The Ghostbusters Record: Structure and Scope
sections.content:
A Ghostbusters Record is an optional signed object that can be associated with any CA certificate in the RPKI. It is verified using an end-entity (EE) certificate issued under the CA certificate. The record's payload is a severely profiled vCard—a minimal version of the standard contact format.

The Ghostbusters Record is not an identity certificate and does not replace resource registry whois data. It attests to contact information made by the CA certificate maintainer. Multiple Ghostbusters Records can be published for a single CA, and they are discovered by walking up the certificate chain to find the nearest CA, then checking its Subject Information Access (SIA) publication point.
sections.plainLanguage: It is a signed sticky note saying "here is how to reach the person who owns this certificate."

sections.title: vCard Profile: Minimal Contact Information
sections.content:
The vCard profile includes only the essential fields: BEGIN and END (the vCard envelope), VERSION (must be 4.0), and FN (the contact name). Required fields are BEGIN, VERSION, FN, and END. To be useful, at least one of ADR (postal address), TEL (phone number), or EMAIL must be included.

Optional fields include ORG (organization name), TEL with type voice, fax, or text, and ADR with structured fields for street, city, state, and country. The profile deliberately excludes properties like PHOTO, URL, or NICKNAME to keep the format simple and the record small.
sections.plainLanguage: The contact card includes your name, organization, phone, email, and mailing address—nothing fancy, just enough to reach you.

sections.title: Trust Model and Privacy Risks
sections.content:
Ghostbusters Records are signed by the CA certificate maintainer, so the data is authenticated. However, the data itself is self-asserted; it has not been independently verified by any other CA or authority. The RFC warns that Ghostbusters Records published on the public Internet are subject to abuse: phone numbers can be targeted for telemarketing or harassment, and email addresses can receive spam.

Operators must weigh the benefit of providing contact information against the privacy risks. The record is optional, and operators can publish zero or more Ghostbusters Records per CA certificate, giving them control over what contact details they expose.
sections.plainLanguage: Anyone can see the contact information, so bad actors might call you with spam or mail spam to your email. It is your choice whether to publish this information.
